candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — skin cancer prevention and self-assessment teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients to use the ABCDE approach to recognize skin lesions that warrant professional evaluation for possible melanoma.

options.A: Assess only whether a lesion is painful and ignore visible changes.
options.B: Assess asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, and whether the lesion is evolving.
options.C: Assess only lesion color because size, shape, and change over time are not useful warning signs.
options.D: Assess only lesions larger than 6 mm and ignore smaller lesions even when they are changing.

candidate.rationale: The American Academy of Dermatology describes the ABCDE warning signs of melanoma as Asymmetry, irregular or poorly defined Border, varying Color, Diameter, and Evolving change. Although melanomas are often larger than 6 mm when diagnosed, they can be smaller, so diameter is not an absolute cutoff. B is the only option that accurately applies the full ABCDE approach.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AAD identifies asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, and evolving change as melanoma warning signs; melanoma can be smaller than 6 mm.
candidate.source_document_title: Melanoma: Signs and symptoms — The ABCDEs of melanoma
